executed_controls.kind: New isolated tests of unchanged original helpers with actual pinned catalog metadata; not original upstream tests or full app search execution.
executed_controls.source_license: MIT; pinned upstream LICENSE already retained and reviewed in repository 013 evidence.
executed_controls.log_normalization: Removed trailing blank line only; test output retained.

findings: Records 80-279 cover touchpad, keyboard, mouse, mobile devices, cameras, printers, Bluetooth, networking and personalization. All description, breadcrumb, name, command, source, synonyms and ID fields read; no launch command executed.
Record 125 embeds a particular USB2.0 HD UVC WebCam model in its label. This is bundled catalog text, not evidence that a target device exists on the current host or that enumeration occurred.

Different private/public Network discovery and File and printer sharing records have distinct IDs and breadcrumbs but the same ms-settings:network-advancedsharing launch target. Three isolated original-helper controls confirm equal launch keys, including a taskbar section versus its Search item.

Original final merge loop discards a result if its ID or nonempty launch key has already appeared. If both tested records reach that merge, only the first remains. This is launch-target deduplication; no full-query ranking, actual Windows navigation or incorrect content-identity behavior is claimed.

Descriptions often name individual state changes, while stored commands navigate to generic settings pages. Labels alone do not prove that toggles, resets, installation or system actions actually execute.
The current file-deduplication library keeps byte-confirmed content groups separate from aliases; the command-key policy is retained only as a research finding, not adopted as file identity.
limits: Catalog semantic review 280/952 records; 262/268 completed files and 155/500 completed repositories unchanged.
No production edit or new performance claim. Previous asset-corpus public API controls remain separate evidence.
